text: Ever wondered how your database finds one row among ten million in the blink of an eye? Meet the database index, the unsung hero working behind the scenes! Think of it like the index at the back of a textbook: instead of flipping through every page to find a topic, you jump straight to the right spot. Under the hood, most indexes use a B-tree, a clever structure that makes lookups O(log n). That means doubling your data adds only one more step to the search, not twice as many. The results can be jaw-dropping. In one real-world case, a query on a 10M-row table dropped from a sluggish 2.1 seconds to just 4 milliseconds. That's a speedup your users will absolutely feel! Of course, every superpower has a tradeoff. Indexes can slow down writes by about 15%, because the database has to keep those shortcuts up to date with every insert and update. So how do you get the best of both worlds? Let's dig into how indexes work, when they shine, and how to use them wisely!
